dedupe_keys.name: mine mining index for natural extremes

description: The Mining Index for Natural Extremes (MINE) combines three climate variables into one index that ranks mining locations by their potential climate risk. It was produced by David Byrne, Dominick Dusseau and Zachary Zobel at the Woodwell Climate Research Center because mining operations, workers and transport links are vulnerable to climate extremes. The variables are extreme rainfall, which can flood mines and trigger landslides that interrupt operations and transport; drought, as a proxy for local water scarcity for water-intensive processing; and heat with humidity, which limits worker productivity. The index is a ranked and weighted average of the three. Version 1.0.0 was published on Zenodo on 18 October 2023 under CC-BY-4.0, with methodology in a documentation file and the generating code in release v1.0.0 of the MINE GitHub repository; the Zenodo record read on 26 September 2026 listed no data files, so the index outputs must be obtained from the repository or the authors. Caveats: it is a relative ranking, not a probability of loss, and depends on the climate projections chosen. For simulation it provides hazard exposure scores for mining assets under climate change and informs adaptation planning of mines and their transport corridors. Related catalogue records include the Global Coal Mine Tracker and the global mining polygons of Maus et al.
